marks.gloss_en: לא קשיא: הא בכולה, הא במקצתה -- the mishnah where all of it was peeled, Rava where part of it was (= p_okimta_mishnah_kulah, p_okimta_rava_miktzatah)
the stam: the mishnah's 'peeled -- unfit' is where all of it was peeled
an etrog pierced with a hole that goes all the way through: at any size
תא שמע: ... תפוח סרוח ... פסול; קתני מיהת תפוח סרוח, מאי לאו: תפוח מבחוץ וסרוח מבפנים -- an etrog decayed within is unfit (= p_mai_lav_mibifnim)
לא, אידי ואידי מבחוץ -- both clauses concern the outside (= p_saruach_mibachutz); the baraita says nothing of decay within
(entertained) is it not that tafuach is [decay] outside and saruach [decay] inside -- so an etrog decayed inside is unfit?
רבי עקיבא -- הא דאמרן; רבי שמעון מאי היא? דתניא: רבי שמעון פוטר את האתרוגים בקוטנן (kind tanya_kevatei: corpus convention, no kind names a bare דתניא)
Rabba: R' Akiva and R' Shimon said one and the same thing
אמר מר: אתרוג כושי פסול. והתניא: כושי כשר, דומה לכושי פסול!
כי תנן נמי מתניתין, דומה לכושי תנן -- the unfit Cushite of the mishnah (and so of the first baraita) is one resembling a Cushite (= p_abaye_domeh_tnan)
לא קשיא: הא לן, והא להו (= p_rava_ha_lan, p_rava_ha_lehu)
the second baraita: a Cushite [etrog] is fit

אמר ליה אביי: דלמא לא היא -- R' Akiva's psul may rest on hadar alone (36a.9), or R' Shimon's exemption on the tithing verse alone (36a.10), each holding like the Rabbis in the other domain; ותו לא מידי (36b.1) -- no answer is given
Abaye (perhaps): R' Akiva says it only here, because we require hadar and there is none; but there [tithes] he holds like the Rabbis
Rava's dilemma: if signs of tereifa arose in an etrog, what is its status -- is it unfit?
a lung poured out like a pitcher -- [the animal] is kosher

Abaye (or else): R' Shimon says it only there, because it is written 'you shall surely tithe all the produce of your seed' -- [produce] as people bring it out for sowing; but here he holds like the Rabbis
